brand.description: Unofficial OpenAPI specifications for ten Power Platform APIs, reverse-engineered and graded by the evidence behind each claim.

grades.title: Verified against the live API
grades.description: Seen on the wire, by probing this service or in recorded first-party traffic.

grades.title: From the admin centre's own client
grades.caveat: A shipped client is strong structural evidence, not an observation.
grades.description: Read from the Power Platform admin centre's JavaScript bundles. A bundle contains every route the client can call, including branches no session exercised, so its coverage is wider than a capture while its confirmation is weaker. It is the most authoritative client for the admin, analytics and athena hosts, which no shipped SDK or PowerShell module touches at all.

grades.title: From Microsoft's own client
grades.caveat: A shipped client is strong structural evidence, not an observation, and the build can be older than the service.
grades.description: Read from Microsoft.PowerPlatform.Management, the Kiota-generated SDK. See each spec's info.x-source-builds for the exact build a claim rests on.

grades.title: From Microsoft's PowerShell admin module
grades.caveat: A shipped client is strong structural evidence, not an observation.
grades.description: Read from Microsoft.PowerApps.Administration.PowerShell, which ships as readable script, so route templates, methods and per-cmdlet api-version defaults are quoted rather than inferred.

grades.title: From a third-party client
grades.caveat: Evidence that an operation exists and is called. Silent about what the service returns.
grades.description: Read from the Terraform provider or another third party's working client. The weakest warrant here and sometimes the only witness: it shows what an operation looks like when somebody uses it in anger, which no vendor artefact does.
